workspace.aria: Agents, models and agent connection (MCP) views

title: Agents
lede: Atlas finds the coding tools already on this computer.
ledeWeb: The desktop app finds the coding tools on this computer and lets you talk to them inside Atlas.

models.lede: Connect the model the conversation beside the map calls.
models.pasteSafety: Your key is stored only in this computer's OS credential store. After saving, no screen can show the full key again (only the last 4 characters). Atlas has no server: the only place this key ever goes is a {provider} API call you explicitly approve.
models.verifyScope: Sends: a minimal auth request → {host} · 0 folder characters · logged
models.verifyNeedsVault: Open a workspace folder first: the record of the call is kept inside that folder.
models.auditEmpty: Nothing sent yet. This file only appears when a call happens.
models.auditPathNote: plain text, so git can read it; whether to commit it is your call
models.webDegradedTitle: Model connections work in the desktop app only.
models.webDegradedBody: A key stored in the browser can be taken by malicious code that reaches the page from another site, so the web build does not offer it. The desktop app puts your key in this computer’s operating-system credential store, and no screen can read the whole key back.
models.localVerified: Pick the model the conversation will use below.
models.localVerifiedWithEmbedding: Only {chat} of these can chat. Pick the model the conversation will use below.
models.localFailUnreachable: No answer from {host}. The runner is off, or the port is different: start it (ollama serve) or fix the address above.
models.localFailNotCompatible: {host} answers, but it is not an OpenAI-compatible API (404). Another program may hold that port, or the runner is too old to expose it: check the port and the runner version.
models.localFailNoModels: Connected, but no models are installed. Pull one (ollama pull qwen3:8b) and check again.
models.localScopeLoopback: Sends: your question + the folder excerpts you picked → {host}. It never leaves this computer, and the log records {host} as the destination: that record is the proof.
models.localScopeRemote: Sends: your question + the folder excerpts you picked → {host}. That address is off this computer, so the log records {host} as the destination.
models.webDegradedLocalBody: Connecting by address to a runner on this computer (Ollama, LM Studio) does not work in the browser either, and changing a setting on the runner does not help: the web build deliberately ships no path for sending text to a model at all. In the desktop app you only type the runner’s address, no key is needed, and the log records this computer as the destination.
models.localTitleHint: Connect by address · no key needed
models.keysTitleHint: Your own keys, kept in the Keychain
models.localOneAtATime: The conversation uses one runner at a time. Connecting this one releases {current}.
models.auditSummary: {count, plural, one {# transfer} other {# transfers}} Atlas sent · all recorded in this folder
models.auditNoVault: Open a folder and every transfer is recorded inside it.

jev.name: Jev evidence check
jev.caption: Shows the request before sending
jev.pasteSafety: Your key is stored only in this computer’s Keychain. It goes to {host} only when you send a check.
jev.intro: Paste one sentence you plan to put in the ontology and the passage meant to support it; Jev says whether the passage supports it. Atlas does not read the folder for you.
jev.claimPlaceholder: For example: a refund request immediately restores inventory.
jev.evidencePlaceholder: For example: after refund approval, a stock-restoration job is queued. (Include the file location.)
jev.requestTitle: Request to send · goes to {host} exactly as shown
jev.requestNote: Atlas records the request’s hash and character counts in this folder first. The key and the text itself are not recorded.
jev.needVault: Open a folder first so the transfer can be recorded.
jev.needBoth: Fill in both the explanation and the passage to send the request.
jev.advisory: Advice only. It does not change or approve the ontology.
jev.experimentalNote: The quality of these answers is not yet verified.
